thought.text: Root returns 200 but all four category pages return 500 due to missing CSV files. Let me examine root page content and confirm the cause.

reasoning_content:
Confirmed: missing CSV files (wachstum-recent.csv, bip-recent.csv, einwohner.csv) that require credentials cause 500 on all pages except `/`. The root `/` returns 200.

Now the question: is this a validation failure? The guide says: yarn install, yarn dev, access at localhost:3000. The app starts, root returns 200. But all four category pages (klima, energie, mobilitaet, abfall) return 500. The dashboard "displays data with various graphs in a tile-based layout, with separate pages for each of the four categories." So the core functionality (category pages) is broken.

The installation summary itself acknowledges: "the data pages /klima, /energie, /mobilitaet return HTTP 500". That's a significant portion of the app. Only the root page works.

Now is this a dependency-installation failure or a missing external credential issue? It's not fixed by installing more npm packages. It requires missing data files (credentials). Per the definitions: "failure: objective evidence demonstrates the resulting installation is incomplete or cannot operate without further installation or repair work." The app cannot operate its main pages without further setup (data files / credentials). 

However, validation boundaries say I cannot repair. But how to distinguish? The installation summary claims only root works. Actually /abfall also 500. So 4 of 5 routes fail.

Let me consider whether the root page truly represents "the application" as operational. The guide says "access the application at localhost:3000". The root returns 200. But main category pages are all 500. The dashboard's stated purpose is to display categories pages.

Let me check the root page more carefully - does it actually render meaningful content, or is it also partially broken? It returned 708KB. Let me check if there's an error in the HTML or if it's the actual dashboard. Also let me check whether root redirects or if the root even contains content.

Let me also verify whether the missing files are truly due to credentials (not something fixable by yarn install). Let me look at the scripts.

Also, an important consideration: maybe the app was previously built (.next exists at 19:11, after install). But the summary said they ran yarn dev and it failed. Actually .next exists from dev runs.

Let me examine the root page content and check whether data creds are the cause.

Let me look at scripts/bip-recent.sh.

action.command: cd /workspace && curl -s --max-time 60 http://localhost:3000/ -o /tmp/root.html; echo "bytes: $(wc -c </tmp/root.html)"; grep -oiE 'Klimadashboard|Münster|<title>[^<]*</title>' /tmp/root.html | head; echo "--- error markers ---"; grep -ciE 'error|module not found|500' /tmp/root.html
